title: Workflows and agents: who owns the control flow?

items.stem: Which statement correctly separates a workflow from an agent?

options.text: A workflow uses tools, while an agent answers from the model's own text
In a workflow the code fixes the steps; in an agent the model picks them
In a workflow the model picks the steps; in an agent the code fixes them
A workflow makes one model call, while an agent makes several fixed ones

items.stem: A makerspace booking feature always runs the same code: (1) ask the model to pull the machine and time out of the student's message, (2) check the calendar for that machine and time, (3) book the slot if it is free, (4) ask the model to write a confirmation. The model never chooses which step comes next. What is this, and why?

options.text: An agent, because it calls tools such as the calendar
An agent, because it calls the model more than once
A workflow, because the code fixes the order of the steps
A workflow, because it makes exactly two model calls

items.stem: Which student request most needs an agent rather than a fixed workflow, because the steps cannot be listed in advance?

options.text: "My 3D print failed twice with stringy output. Find out why and see if the printer is free to retry."
"Book the laser cutter for Friday at 2 pm, and confirm it to me by message."
"What time does the makerspace open on weekdays, and when does it close?"
"Remind every student who has a booking tomorrow about their time slot."

items.stem: The booking steps in q2 are known in advance and always the same. Give one reason, in a sentence, why a fixed workflow is a better choice than an agent for them, given the team's small model budget.

A fixed workflow handles each booking request with 2 model calls. An agent handling the same request makes 4 model calls on average (three tool requests plus the final answer). For 150 booking requests, how many more model calls does the agent make than the workflow? Assume every call costs the same and ignore differences in prompt length.
A teammate says: "The assistant calls the calendar tool, so it must be an agent." What is the best reply?

options.text: Right, because any system that calls a tool is an agent
Right, as long as the calendar tool is called more than once
Wrong, because an agent must also remember students between sessions
Wrong, because code can call tools in a fixed order; an agent is when the model chooses
